sources.role: joystick profile parser/printer, SDL3 physical-device grammar, config and snapshot implementation
official XRoar platform paths, firmware, media, joystick and snapshot documentation

paths.naming: XRoar reads one directive per line; -config-auto-save writes the user configuration here. Joystick profiles use joy, joy-axis, joy-button, joy-right and joy-left directives.

The config can define named joystick profiles and map physical:<device>,<axis> or physical:<device>,%<button-mask>; SDL device numbers are current enumeration order and require same-launch measurement.
XRoar reads and writes virtual cassette and floppy images at the caller-supplied paths; the emulator does not define a universal game-save sidecar.
evidence: source:xroar@0229f97a src/xroar.c media and disk modules

paths.path: User-selected .sna snapshot path (or .ram for RAM-only snapshot)
paths.naming: Ctrl+S writes an XRoar snapshot and Ctrl+L recognises .sna; snapshots preserve machine state but external ROM/media files must remain available at their original paths.
Firmware is supplied as machine-named ROM images, including d32.rom, d64_1.rom, coco3.rom/coco3p.rom and disk11.rom (disk10.rom optional for RS-DOS).
evidence: source:xroar@0229f97a README and src/xroar.c ROM lists

linux-flatpak.reason: The pinned XRoar source documents native Linux, Windows and macOS paths but publishes no authoritative Flatpak package or sandbox persistence contract.

controller_boundary.refusal: The writer appends only source-defined joy/joy-axis/joy-button/joy-right/joy-left declarations and requires a same-launch SDL enumeration index; it must not claim stable device identity or runtime-verified controller behavior.

notes: XRoar's native writer is source-shaped but writer-only: ROM, media and snapshot paths remain caller-owned, and SDL device order remains a runtime boundary.
